item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Aug 8, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Aug 12, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Philosophy | Drink | Film at Zoetropolis: Moonlight — Thu Aug 20, 6:30 PM — Zoetropolis Cinema Stillhouse
item.description:
PDF@Zoetropolis presents Barry Jenkins’ Moonlight. The next film in our America 250 series—and the second in our three-film exploration of Reinvention and Transformation.
Told across three defining periods in one life, Moonlight follows Chiron as he grows up in Miami and struggles with the names others give him, the expectations of masculinity, and his longing to be known. Visually breathtaking and deeply humane, the film explores identity, race, sexuality, vulnerability, and the rare moments of tenderness that make another way of living possible. America celebrates the self-made individual—but who is truly free to reinvent themselves? And what happens when the identity we construct to survive becomes a form of armor?

item.description:
Historic Rock Ford’s America250 Lecture Series presents “Walls That Witnessed a Revolution: Lancaster County Before 1776” in which Danielle Keperling explores the pre-1776 buildings throughout Lancaster County.
This presentation will begin at 6 PM in the Langmuir Education Room located on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. Admission is for the lecture only and does not include the Snyder Gallery or Hand Mansion.
About the Presenter: Danielle Keperling serves as the Executive Director of the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County, where she advances preservation advocacy, education, and stewardship across the county. She also serves on the Lancaster City Historical Commission, helping oversee the Heritage Conservation District.

item.title: The Great American Tour at American Music Theatre — Sun Aug 9, 3:00 PM — American Music Theatre
item.description: The Great American Tour is a celebration of the timeless music that defined a generation—and continues to resonate today. Baby Boomers have never lost their passion for the “oldies but goodies” of the 1960s and 70s, and this unforgettable show delivers the songs that shaped youth, freedom, and the unifying power of rock ’n roll. Featuring iconic artists inducted into the Vocal Group Hall of Fame, this tour brings together legendary performers whose hits remain woven into modern movies, television, and commercials, captivating audiences across generations. Headlining the tour are Jay and the Americans, one of the era’s few groups still featuring two original members. With an incredible legacy that includes 19 charted hits and 9 Top 40 records, the group continues to thrive with over 900,000 monthly Spotify listeners. item.title: Evening Compline — Sun Aug 9, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.description:
[vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”907737″]Join us at Millport Conservancy for an unforgettable Perseid Meteor Shower Stargazing Party—right during its dazzling peak. Get ready for one of the most spectacular sky shows of the year! When: Wednesday, August 12 | 8 PM–11 PM Where: Millport Conservancy, Lititz, PA. Just minutes from Lancaster—yet light-years away from skyglow! Cost: FREE The Perseid meteor shower is famous for producing up to 100 meteors per hour, including brilliant fireballs—flashes of light so bright they can rival Venus in the night sky. These “shooting stars” seem to originate from the constellation Perseus in the northeastern sky, and will be visible with the naked eye, even amidst some lunar light pollution. What to Expect:
